items.text: Persepolis club announced it intends to pursue the case regarding Yaser Asani's presence in Esteghlal's lineup at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) after the Football Federation's Appeals Committee rejected their complaint. Persepolis stated that international follow-up of the case had previously been approved by the board, and now with the Appeals Committee's ruling, the next steps of the complaint are underway. A meeting is scheduled on Wednesday with club managers and legal advisors to review legal aspects and expedite preparation of the complaint for referral to CAS.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, criticized the referee's performance after his team's 2-0 loss to Shabab Al Ahli UAE in the AFC Champions League, attributing the difference between the teams to their use of scoring opportunities. He apologized to the fans and said the team had faced tough matches recently. Bakhtiarizadeh also defended Esteghlal's more defensive play and strongly criticized the match officiating.

After the polls closed in Israel on the evening of Tuesday, 5 Aban, some citizens and party supporters in various locations, including Tel Aviv, took to the streets and celebrated alongside the announcement of probable results. These polls indicate a close competition with no definitive winner. Vote counting continues and the final result announcement may take several days.

Gadi Eizenkot, leader of the Yesh Atid party in Israel, considered the exit poll results from the parliamentary elections on Tuesday, 5 Aban, as a sign of the majority of Israeli citizens' vote of no confidence in Benjamin Netanyahu and his government. He promised to act to replace Netanyahu's government and form a Zionist government committed to universal mandatory military service. According to initial polls, the opposition coalition to Netanyahu is ahead of his supporting coalition, but neither coalition has reached the majority of 61 seats needed to form a government.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said the Islamic Republic hopes Benjamin Netanyahu will lose in the Israeli elections because it fears his continued cooperation with Donald Trump against Tehran. Vaisi added that in recent months, the Islamic Republic has tried to influence the US midterm elections by intensifying attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and raising oil prices. He also said Netanyahu's possible departure is more psychologically significant for the regime and that the final election result depends on vote counting and coalition negotiations.

Initial exit poll estimates in the Israeli parliamentary elections indicate that neither of the two main political blocs has secured the majority needed to form a government. The coalition led by Benjamin Netanyahu is estimated to win between 50 and 60 seats, while opposition parties are estimated to win between 43 and 52 seats out of 120 Knesset seats. These results indicate a political deadlock as neither Netanyahu nor his rival has a clear path to form a government.

The HalVash human rights group reported, by publishing videos, that armed individuals attacked the Relief Unit headquarters and Police Station 11 in Khash on Tuesday, October 27, and heavy clashes and shooting, including with machine guns, continued for over an hour. According to HalVash, local sources reported that a number of military forces were killed and injured, and official authorities have not yet announced any statistics on the number of dead and injured.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel, said that confronting the threats of the Islamic Republic and weakening its capabilities is a common point among Israel's main political currents. He added that part of the plans to confront Tehran were designed during the terms of Naftali Bennett and Gadi Eisenkot, and the parties' disagreements are mostly about how to implement these policies. Sabti also said that Benjamin Netanyahu's political behavior and humiliating treatment of his opponents have helped unite his rivals, and he did not rule out the possibility of Netanyahu forming a new coalition, but emphasized that the election results and negotiations among parties will determine the composition of Israel's future government.

Kambiz Tavana, a reporter for Iran International, said that discrepancies among exit polls in the Israeli elections have made predicting the composition of the future government difficult. He added that the formation of the government by Benjamin Netanyahu or his opponents, as well as the possibility of a political deadlock, remain topics of discussion. Tavana emphasized that the final result depends on the vote count and coalition negotiations, and it is still unclear who will form the future government.

Meir Javdanfar said that if the Islamic Republic falls, diplomatic relations between Iran and Israel could be quickly established, and Turkey and Qatar are concerned about this development. He added that the Israeli people's view of Iranians is positive and the historical and cultural ties between the two nations remain important. Javdanfar also said that Gadi Eizenkot needs to reach agreements with other parties, including Arab parties, to form a government, and the possible presence of Arab parties could change Israel's diplomatic image, but political disagreements and opposition from Haredi factions to military service will be major challenges for the government.

In today's Israeli parliamentary elections, Benjamin Netanyahu faced Gadi Eisenkot, the former Chief of Staff of the Israeli army. Eisenkot has gained more support in polls in recent months. His party has become one of the main rivals of the Likud party.

Mike Waltz, the US representative to the United Nations, addressed corruption in the Cuban government during the UN General Assembly, mentioning issues such as "luxury watches" and the private island "Cayo Piedra." These remarks provoked a strong reaction from the Cuban delegation, who protested by banging on the table. Khalil al-Rahman, the President of the General Assembly, suspended the session briefly following these reactions.

Reuters reported that Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, is expected to face questions about Washington's commitment to its obligations in the Indo-Pacific region during his meeting with counterparts from Southeast Asian countries in the Philippines on Wednesday, 6 Aban. The Iran war has pressured US military readiness and tensions between the Philippines and China in the South China Sea have increased. Analysts said Southeast Asian countries may use the meeting with Hegseth to clarify US goals in the Iran war and its impact on Washington's commitments in the region.

Donald Trump said in a campaign speech in Texas that the war with Iran will end whenever he wants and emphasized that the war will end soon. He added that it must be ensured that the world's biggest supporter of terrorism never obtains nuclear weapons. Trump has previously repeatedly spoken about the war's imminent end and stressed that the Islamic Republic should not acquire nuclear weapons.

The latest exit polls of the Israeli elections indicate an improvement in Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition position. Channel 12 reported the lead of Netanyahu's supporting coalition, while Channels 11 and 13 predicted a tie between the two main coalitions. Neither side has reached the majority needed to form a government.

An oil slick caused by damage to an oil tanker off the coast of the United Arab Emirates has expanded, leading to the closure of more beaches. Videos published on social media on October 26 and 27 show a closed beach in Ras Al Khaimah. Authorities in the emirate had announced on Saturday that all its beaches would be closed until further notice.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, after the release of exit poll results in the parliamentary elections, said Israel faces a historic opportunity to eliminate the threat of the Islamic Republic. He stated that the right-wing coalition has gained a decisive majority and that Iran is weaker than ever. Netanyahu also said Israel, together with Donald Trump, will end the threat from Iran once and for all.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US has informed several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a possible short but intense military operation against the Islamic Republic after the US midterm elections. The newspaper wrote that the US military is moving a Patriot missile system from Texas to strengthen its missile defense and relocating forces from vulnerable bases. Also, Donald Trump has not made a final decision but favors a large-scale attack after the elections that could target Iran's infrastructure and nuclear facilities.

Exit poll results published by Israel's Channel 12, Channel 14, and i24 News indicate the lead of Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, but there is an eight-seat discrepancy regarding the number of seats for this coalition. According to Channel 14's poll, Netanyahu's coalition will win 60 out of 120 Knesset seats. However, none of these polls show Netanyahu's coalition reaching the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government alone.

The first exit polls in the Israeli parliamentary elections show that opposition parties to Netanyahu win 52 to 53 seats, and his supporting coalition wins about 50 seats; thus, neither camp reaches the 61-seat threshold to form a government.

Erfan Ghaneifard, a Middle East analyst, says that a change of government in Israel may alter the timing, intensity, and method of operations against the Islamic Republic, but it does not fundamentally change Israel's security strategy towards Tehran. He states that confronting the missile and nuclear programs of the Islamic Republic and its security threats is pursued beyond electoral calculations and party politics in Israel.

Sadegh Beigdeli said that although the Israeli Prime Minister can influence tactics and some important decisions, the main strategy of Israel towards the Islamic Republic will not fundamentally change with a change of government. He added that currently, the Israeli army and security agencies such as Mossad and Shin Bet have a more prominent role in decision-making.

Kambiz Tavana, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the meeting between Masoud Pezeshkian and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, despite discussing energy cooperation, did not lead to a tangible agreement in this area. According to him, the only announced agreement was the reopening of the Russian state network VGTRK's office in Tehran, and there was no clear sign of practical action by Moscow to help Tehran against US economic pressures.

Prisoners participating in the "Tuesdays Against Execution" campaign went on a hunger strike in 66 prisons across Iran during the 144th week of the campaign. According to the campaign's statement, at least 87 people have been executed in Iran in the past 20 days, including seven political prisoners and two women. An interview with Pegah Bani Hashemi, a senior legal researcher at the University of Chicago, discussed the increase in execution rates and concerns of activists and human rights organizations.

The Parliament of South Australia held a ceremony to commemorate those who lost their lives for freedom in Iran. Parliament members condemned the suppression of protesters by the Islamic Republic during the ceremony. They called for an end to executions and the release of political prisoners.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations instructor, said that the pressure from the midterm congressional elections and rising energy prices could affect Donald Trump's decisions regarding the Islamic Republic. He stated that Trump might, after the elections, push Tehran to accept a deal either through negotiation or increased military pressure. Qaedi also considered the acceptance of zero percent enrichment by the Islamic Republic as a factor facilitating the agreement, but he assessed this scenario as very unlikely.

Donald Trump said Iran wanted to make a deal but may be waiting for elections, and elections will not help them. He added that their military power has been crushed and their financial resources severely weakened. Trump also said Iran's inflation rate is now 340 percent.

Australia's News24 network reported exclusively that cyber agents linked to the IRGC accessed emails and personal information of Sherry Markson, the network's presenter. Australia's intelligence and security agency also confirmed that agents linked to the Islamic Republic targeted two prominent figures in the country with intelligence operations this year.

Abdolali Arzhang, the political and security deputy governor of Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, said Esmail Eslami Babahaidari, the mayor of Jonqan in Farsan County, was targeted in an armed attack early Wednesday, 6 Aban, and was killed by gunfire. Arzhang told Fars News Agency that initial assessments indicate the incident did not have security dimensions. No further details have been released about how the attack occurred or the identity of the perpetrator(s).

In the early morning of Tuesday, 5 Aban, the execution of a prisoner was carried out in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. The prisoner had previously been sentenced to death on charges related to drug crimes.

Mansheh Amir, a Middle East expert, said it is still early to judge the final result of the Israeli elections and the formation of a new government. He added that Netanyahu will try to form a coalition of 61 seats and may offer concessions to gain the support of Arab parties. Amir also emphasized that Netanyahu's positions on overthrowing the Islamic Republic and his cooperation with Donald Trump are important in considering Israel's future policy towards Tehran.

Hossein Alizadeh, an international affairs analyst, called Donald Trump's statements about the Islamic Republic starting a war unprecedented and said this stance is more understandable within the framework of US electoral competition than as a legal claim. He pointed to political pressures on Trump due to the US entering a war and said the US president tries to attribute the responsibility for starting the conflict to the Islamic Republic.

Serbia's Interior Minister announced that early Wednesday, an unidentified individual attacked a security officer guarding the Israeli embassy in Belgrade with two knives. According to him, the assailant shouted "Allahu Akbar" during the attack, and the officer killed him in self-defense. The Interior Minister also stated that security agencies had previously been monitoring this individual and, based on initial information, he was a supporter of the ISIS group.

With over 57% of the votes counted in the Israeli parliamentary elections, the coalition supporting Benjamin Netanyahu has won 55 seats and the opposition coalition 49 seats. Two mainly Arab parties have won a total of 16 seats. No coalition has reached a parliamentary majority.

Arsenal was eliminated from the EFL Cup after losing on penalties to Fleetwood Town, a fourth-tier English football team. The defeat was accompanied by the sending off of 16-year-old Arsenal player Max Dowman and a sharp reaction from Mikel Arteta. Dowman was sent off with a straight red card after receiving a heavy tackle, and Arteta spoke angrily to him as he left the field.

Turkey-Israel relations have reached their lowest level due to disagreements over Gaza, Syria, and regional security. The future of relations depends on the new Israeli government's policies regarding these issues.

Artin Ghazanfari, a Baháʼí citizen and photojournalist, was sentenced to 26 years in prison by Judge Abolghasem Salavati. His physical condition has been reported as poor, and despite suffering from heart failure, high blood pressure, and asthma, he has been denied transfer to medical centers outside the prison. This information was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The first women's football derby in Iran between Esteghlal and Persepolis was supposed to be a historic celebration, but changes in time and venue, repeated suspension of ticket sales, a ban on men's presence, and intervention by the Tehran prosecutor turned the event into a new scene of gender discrimination in the Islamic Republic of Iran. The match was moved from the 1st of Aban to the 6th of Aban, and ticket sales were stopped twice. The final decision on women's attendance at the stadium was left to the Tehran Provincial Security Council.

Tasnim News Agency reported that on the morning of Wednesday, 6 Aban, a collision between a trailer and a minibus carrying students in Ardakan, Yazd province, resulted in one student killed and 12 others injured. The head of Ziaei Hospital in Ardakan stated that 13 students were in the minibus and the condition of three injured is critical. The secretary of Ardakan Crisis Management Headquarters said the accident occurred around 8 AM and attributed the cause to the minibus blocking the way.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, wrote on the social network X that Iran's energy diplomacy took a step forward at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit. He stated that developments in global gas markets and energy security were the main focus of discussions at this summit. Araghchi added that the harmful consequences of any military adventurism incited by Israel in the Persian Gulf region for international markets remain a serious concern for gas exporting and consuming countries.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said that the Islamic Republic has long sought an agreement with Washington but continues to try to prolong the negotiation process. He added that Tehran may be waiting for the results of the midterm congressional elections, but these elections will not help the Islamic Republic.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, said that revenge against the US and Israel for the killing of the former leader of the Islamic Republic is certain and the perpetrators must expect "severe punishment." He also emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz will not be reopened until the full acceptance and implementation of the Islamic Republic's conditions.

European media have reported the possibility of a continued political crisis, increased role of Arab parties, and difficulties in forming a replacement government following the Israeli parliamentary elections. The continuation of Netanyahu's premiership during the transitional period has also raised questions about the future of Israel's foreign and security policy, especially regarding Iran and the European Union.

The Argentine government says that Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, has traveled through Argentina to Ecuador and is on his way to the United States. Reports indicate that Donald Trump has approved granting him a US visa, and Bolsonaro intends to seek asylum in the United States.

Iran International audiences from various cities in Iran say they are following the Israeli parliamentary elections and hope for the victory of Benjamin Netanyahu's party. The elections are being followed while, according to the audiences, supporters of the government are also awaiting Netanyahu's defeat.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic remains unable to decide its stance with the US and faces two paths: accepting Washington's demands or confronting serious internal changes. He referred to recent positions of Donald Trump and statements by Abbas Araghchi about regional countries, warning that continuing tension policies could increase the risk of war.

The women's football teams of Esteghlal and Persepolis face each other today in the first derby of the women's Premier League history. Persepolis enters the match as the leader and undefeated, while Esteghlal seeks to gain points to approach the contenders. Esteghlal club released a video from their women's team camp where players talk about their feelings about participating in the first women's football derby in Iran and express hope for victory against Persepolis.

The deputy of school renovation in Lorestan reported the identification of about 30 stone schools in the province and claimed that the organization of container schools with more than 10 students has largely been completed. Abdi also mentioned a tent school in the village of Gereh Shir Takht Cho in Pol Dokhtar county, stating that this school provides a tent space for educating nomadic tribal students and currently has only two students.
Abdolaziz Azimi Ghadim, a 52-year-old Azerbaijani activist, has been transferred from Evin Prison to Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters that the Islamic Republic's policy of showing no flexibility on the nuclear issue remains unchanged. He also emphasized that Qatar has not yet presented a new proposal to end the war between the Islamic Republic and the US. The official said that the ideas presented by Doha are not acceptable to the Islamic Republic.

Navid Toubian, a senior Iranian researcher at the Memri Institute, said that despite Donald Trump's popularity in Israel, the impact of his support on the election outcome is unclear. He suggested that Netanyahu's electoral warnings about increased Arab participation might have had the opposite effect. Toubian emphasized that it is too early to judge the possibility of Netanyahu forming a government until the remaining votes, including soldiers' votes, are counted.
It was reported that following gunfire by military forces in the Kohnooj area, a fuel smuggler's vehicle overturned and the driver died.

Ali Al-Zaidi, Prime Minister of Iraq, traveled to Damascus for an official meeting with Ahmad Al-Shara, President of Syria. The discussions focus on expanding economic relations, combating terrorism, and strengthening the security of shared borders.

A video of Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, before meeting Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin Palace has become popular on social media. In this video, Pezeshkian, while getting out of the car, stamps his foot on the ground in front of a Kremlin protocol official. This brief moment has received widespread reactions from users on social media.

The Deputy Operations Officer of the Rahvar Police announced that over 80% of Tehran's taxi fleet is worn out and the renewal process is slow. He also stated that over 74% of city buses are aged and that these worn-out vehicles contribute to air pollution and reduced safety.

Branch 15 of Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced Artin Ghazanfari, a photojournalist and Bahá'í citizen, to 26 years in prison. The sentence was communicated to him on Monday, 5 Aban, at Tehran Grand Prison. He was sentenced to 20 years for "media action" with aggravated punishment, five years for "assembly and collusion," and one year for "propaganda against the regime."

Iranian state news agencies and media, including Fars, Tasnim, Entekhab, Daneshjoo, IRNA, Mehr, and the IRIB news agency, are extensively covering the Israeli parliamentary elections, broadcasting news, statistics, poll results, and statements from various factions live and moment by moment.

Reports from Zarindasht, Shiraz, Tehran, and Arak indicate severe price increases and declining quality of goods and services. Cabinet makers have stopped working due to high costs, new tolls have been imposed at Siros Crossroad in Tehran, and prices of internet and insulin have risen sharply. People complain about poor internet quality and economic difficulties.

A journalist inside Iran told Iran International that the Israeli elections have become a topic of conversation among people in shops, stores, buses, and the metro. The journalist said they saw citizens who have made vows for the Israeli elections. Also, some citizens wistfully compare the presence of various parties, frank criticism of government policies, and media freedom in Israel with the situation in Iran.

Mohammad Ghorbani and Mobin Dehghan, two Iranian players of Al Wahda UAE, have not been allowed to travel to Bahrain for the match against Al Khalidiya in the AFC Champions League. Bahraini authorities opposed the entry of these two Iranian players, which caused the Al Wahda coach to protest. The club officials are negotiating to lift this restriction, but it is still unclear if the two players will participate in the Wednesday match.

Kuwait's Foreign Ministry announced on Wednesday, 6 Aban, that it summoned Mohammad Toutounji, the ambassador of the Islamic Republic in the country, and delivered a protest note to him. The ministry stated that the statement by the Iranian embassy contained "clear interference" in Kuwait's internal affairs and an affront to the sovereignty and independence of Kuwait's judiciary. Kuwait's Deputy Foreign Minister condemned any interference in the rulings issued by the country's courts and called on the Islamic Republic to adhere to international laws, the UN Charter, the principle of non-interference in internal affairs, and the Vienna Convention on diplomatic relations.

Messages received by Iran International indicate audience anger over the increase in internet prices. Some have said they have limited their presence on social networks to reduce costs, and others say they have to pay more due to the need for internet.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said Mojtaba Khamenei has "fully regained his health" and now receives reports and plans from officials of the three branches of government. He added that Khamenei secretly attends some public gatherings and observes them closely.

As the vote count in the Israeli elections continues, some Iranian users are concerned about the consequences of the result, and some have posted humorous reactions supporting Benjamin Netanyahu. A group has also written that after Netanyahu, support should be given to Trump.

A report was given on the living conditions and economic crisis in Iran on Wednesday, 6 Aban. It was stated that internet package prices have increased but internet speed is low, and neighboring countries of Iran are closing routes, disrupting imports and exports. It was also mentioned that retirees' overdue salaries were paid but the amount was very low.

A senior Islamic Republic official told Reuters that Qatar has not yet presented a new proposal. The official described Doha's ideas as unacceptable and emphasized that the Islamic Republic's policy of showing no flexibility on the nuclear issue has not changed. Reuters had earlier reported the presentation of a draft Qatar agreement in Tehran.
The police commander of Khansar reported the arrest of a citizen in this city for reasons including insulting religious sanctities in cyberspace.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, called on parties to form a coalition and prevent a new election following the preliminary election results. He said that next week, after receiving the official results, consultations to form the government will begin.

Nemat Afshar, a resident of Qazvin, was arrested on Monday, 4 Aban, by the Intelligence Force agents in the city and transferred to an unknown location. Harana reported that his arrest took place at his residence. His family is unaware of the reason for the arrest and his whereabouts and is concerned.

Preliminary results of the Israeli parliamentary elections have received extensive coverage in Arab media. Al-Araby Al-Jadeed newspaper highlighted the role of Arab parties in the future Israeli government. Canadian media also reported that the enthusiastic participation of Arab citizens of Israel and traditional right-wingers will be decisive.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the election results in Israel could change the government and the dominant power faction, but in the Islamic Republic, power shifts among government factions.
According to a received video, a group of workers from the Gachsaran Oil and Gas Exploitation Company held a protest gathering on Tuesday, 5 Aban, against their labor issues.

A hearing on the charges against Siamak Sadeghi Chehrazi, a teachers' union activist and board member of the Khuzestan Teachers' Union, was held on Wednesday, 6 Aban, at Branch One of the Ahvaz Revolutionary Court. He is accused of propaganda against the regime and insulting Hassan Nasrallah on social media. The Coordination Council of Iranian Cultural Workers' Unions emphasized the necessity of respecting the legal rights of union activists and fair trial rights.

According to information received by Iran International, Ehsan Abedini, 35 years old, was killed on 18 Dey in Sattarkhan Street, Tehran, by gunfire from the suppressive forces of the Islamic Republic. Danial, his 23-year-old brother, died 12 days later and Reza, their father, died a few months later from a heart attack.

A report from Harana about structural problems in the electricity industry that have caused skilled workers to be deprived of their real wages. The issue goes beyond contractors and relates to a structure where intermediaries take a large share of the work's value. These workers are still waiting for basic rights and economic security.

Israel Katz, Israel's defense minister, accused Gadi Eisenkot and his allies of spreading misinformation about disagreements between Israeli political and military officials over Iran and emphasized that the army participates in all decision-making. Katz wrote that the army has fully participated in "major achievements" against the Islamic Republic and is currently present in all discussions. He also described Eisenkot's stance on commanders not following orders from the prime minister and defense minister as undemocratic.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, said all efforts must be made to prevent holding new elections and expects representatives and political parties to enter consultations with an open mind. He described the widespread public participation in the elections as remarkable and said this level of participation was unprecedented in decades. Herzog stated he will receive the official results next week and will begin consultations with various parties.

With the counting of the majority of votes in the Israeli parliamentary elections, Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition has won the most seats. This coalition, with 53 seats, is ahead of the opposition coalition led by Gadi Eisenkot. Parties representing Arab citizens have also set an unprecedented record by winning 19 seats.

Israel Hayom newspaper reported on Wednesday, 6 Aban, quoting a senior diplomatic official that US and Israeli efforts regarding Iran, including the possibility of resuming military attacks, will continue independently of the formation of the new Israeli government, and the election results will not affect military and intelligence cooperation between the two sides. The senior diplomatic official said that military, intelligence, and diplomatic cooperation between Washington and Jerusalem remains close and strong, and decisions about next actions will be based solely on the shared interests of the US and Israel. He emphasized that if a renewed attack on Iran is deemed necessary, the decision will be made solely on professional considerations, and the US midterm election results will not change Washington and Israel's strategic calculations regarding Iran.

Richard Peter, executive director of the UK-Israel Communications and Research Center, said the United Arab List in the previous coalition has shown it can be a reliable partner. He considered the presence of this party in the future government as one of the possible scenarios.
A video received by Iran International shows that a group of drivers from Damavand Energy Petrochemical Company in Asaluyeh stopped working and went on strike in protest against their low wages.

Israel's Likud party stated that Arab parties "supporting terrorism" committed widespread election fraud using bribery, threats, violence, cheating, and banned software, altering the election results. Likud said it is submitting evidence including thousands of cash envelopes and Ra'am party ballots, threats and violence against polling station members, and dual identity voting to the police and security agencies.

Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, expressed special thanks to Gholamhossein Mohseni-Eje'i, head of the judiciary, during the World Wrestling Championships. He said Mohseni-Eje'i showed emotional care and support for the athletes. However, questions have been raised about executions and widespread arrests of athletes during Mohseni-Eje'i's tenure.

Scott Busent, the US Treasury Secretary, said Iran's economy has been in recession for 47 years due to decisions by the Islamic Republic, and Turkey's economy is now several times larger. He added that if Tehran abandons its pursuit of nuclear weapons, Iran could become one of the most successful countries in the world.

Seyed Ahmad Seyed Abdollahi, a political prisoner, was released today, Wednesday, 6 Aban, under electronic monitoring from Borujen prison. He will serve the remainder of his sentence outside prison with travel restrictions. His five-year ban from all public and social services remains in effect.

Donald Trump spoke about the results of the Israeli parliamentary elections, saying he initially received "terrible" reports about Netanyahu's electoral prospects, but now the Israeli Prime Minister is "in a relatively good position." Trump added that he heard his support for Netanyahu had a significant impact. He said he has not yet thought about intervening to form a unity government but will consider it.

A released video shows the mother of the deceased Armin Teymouri-rad joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" by lighting a candle for her son. Armin Teymouri-rad, 19 years old, was killed on the evening of 19 Dey in Fardis.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said the country will stand in any situation and the current conditions can be an opportunity to increase resilience. He emphasized that the current threat is a compulsion and there is no choice. Pezeshkian added that spaces can be closed and preparations can be made for the current situation.

The Central Elections Committee of Israel announced that it has received the Likud party's request regarding allegations of widespread fraud by Arab parties and will review it within the framework of election integrity oversight. The committee emphasized that reviewing parties' requests about possible violations and the accuracy of election results is part of the usual oversight process. Also, Din Lione, the acting CEO of the committee, contacted parties about the process of reviewing possible election violations two days before the elections.

Niloufar Ardalan, head coach of Persepolis women's team, after the first women's football derby in Iran and a 2-1 victory over Esteghlal, said: "We achieved a historic win for Persepolis. It's a pity this match was not broadcast live. Even the club managers could not watch the game in person."

One day after the Israeli elections, it is still unclear which coalition will form the next government. Netanyahu's coalition has won 53 seats and Gadi Eizenkot's coalition has won 48 seats, and neither has reached the 61-seat threshold. Arab parties, having won 19 seats, could play a decisive role in forming the government.

Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, claimed on Wednesday, 6 Aban, that last year's Dey protests in Iran started from social networks. According to the Russian news agency Interfax, Putin said these networks were neither managed nor controlled by Iranian authorities, and the only action they could take was to cut everything off.

Na'im Qasim, Secretary-General of Hezbollah Lebanon, stated that they value the agreement between Iran and the US because it is, alongside resistance, the only source of power. He said the Islamic Republic prioritizes stopping Israeli attacks on Lebanon and the withdrawal of Israeli forces. Qasim also said the results of the Israeli elections are a sign of failure and it does not matter to them who leads Israel.
On Monday, 4 Aban, Ahmad Iranmanesh, a citizen from Saravan County, was arrested by security forces in this county and transferred to an unknown location.

The United Nations General Assembly is holding a meeting on the human rights crisis in Iran. In this meeting, Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights, and the independent international fact-finding committee will present their reports.

Ben Sabti, a researcher on Iran and Israel issues, said the alignments are still unclear and the remaining votes need to be counted. He suggested the possibility of religious parties joining Netanyahu's rivals and said some Likud members might join the opposition to prevent a repeat election.

Persepolis women's football team defeated Esteghlal 2-1 in the first derby of the Iranian Women's Premier League and won this historic match. The match had various controversies; male spectators and journalists were banned from entering the stadium, and both clubs were not allowed to broadcast the match live.

Meir Javdanfar said Benjamin Netanyahu still has loyal support from a significant portion of voters despite widespread criticism. He predicted Netanyahu might use a new war against Iran to maintain power, but it is unlikely he will form the next government. Javdanfar considered the coalition of Gadi Eizenkot with Arab parties more likely and called it a historic achievement for Israel.

Reuters reported on Wednesday, 6 Aban that Qatari mediators presented a new draft agreement to Iran to end the war with the United States and Israel, but a senior Islamic Republic official said Doha only proposed "unacceptable" ideas and they cannot be considered an "offer." An informed official said the draft includes a seven-day timeline for confidence-building, and Iran's response is expected by the end of the week.

With over 85% of votes counted in the Israeli election, none of the factions have secured the necessary parliamentary majority to form a government. An interview with Arash Azizi, a history researcher and humanities lecturer at Yale University.

Jamshid Molaei, Esmail Molaei, Hossein Molaei, Armin Molaei, and Aref Dadvand, citizens of Izeh, have been held in judicial limbo in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz for over 70 days. Since their arrest, they have been deprived of phone contact and visits with their families. Jamshid, Esmail, and Hossein Molaei are relatives of Kian Pirfalak, a child killed during the nationwide protests of 1401.

Technical structure workers of Travers Company criticized the payment of only 75% of their October salaries. They say their salaries have been paid incompletely and with delay for several months and demand full payment of salaries and benefits every month.

United Students reported that Nabi Omidi, an associate professor of economics and financial management at Payame Noor University, has been sentenced to 9 years in prison, five years of which are enforceable, for his presence and support of the January 2027 protests in Malekshahi county. According to the report, he faced charges of "acting against national security," "propaganda against the system," and participation in protests. In addition to imprisonment, dismissal from the university, a travel ban, confiscation of his passport, and a ban on entering Malekshahi county have been announced as supplementary punishments for this university professor.
A citizen told Iran International in a video that each carton of electrodes has reached a price of 8,200,000 tomans, mentioning the rising prices and work stoppages in Iran.

A report states that the execution of a prisoner convicted of intentional murder in a group fight case was carried out in Kashan prison in Khordad. Also, three prisoners sentenced to death in Dargaz, Nishapur, and Dandi were released after the victims' families pardoned them. The General Directorate of Prisons in Isfahan province announced that 27 death penalty cases were settled in the first half of the current year.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that despite decades of propaganda and huge expenses to create hatred against Israel, the Islamic Republic has not achieved its goal. He also referred to the sympathy of Iranians with the people of Israel after the October 7 attack and their sensitivity to developments in that country.

Hadi Jamalipour, a political prisoner serving his sentence on furlough, was dismissed from his workplace. He was previously an employee at Payame Noor University in Birjand. A source close to his family confirmed that in Mehr month of this year, Jamalipour was dismissed by an order from the disciplinary council of Payame Noor University.
A released video shows the family of the late Arman Abed Moghami holding his birthday anniversary ceremony at his grave. Arman Abed Moghami, 35 years old, was killed in Rasht on 18 Dey 1404.

According to The Wall Street Journal, the US has warned Gulf countries to be prepared for the possibility of a short but intense military campaign in Iran after next week's midterm elections. Washington is also strengthening air defenses, supplying ammunition, and preparing fighter jets and bombers in the region.

Meir Javedanfar, an analyst on Israeli affairs, considered the winning of 27 seats by Likud as a sign of Netanyahu maintaining his voter base. He suggested Netanyahu might use a new war against Iran to retain power, but found it unlikely that Netanyahu would form the government and considered an Eisenkot coalition with Arab parties more probable.
Idris Mohammadzadeh, a citizen from Mahabad, was arrested on Saturday, 2 Aban, for the execution of a five-year and one-day prison sentence and was transferred to Mahabad prison.

Hossein Ahmadi, a detainee linked to the nationwide protests of Dey 1404, remains in legal limbo after 166 days of detention in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. He suffers from physical problems in his back and neck and has been deprived of proper medical care and transfer to medical centers. This report was published by HRANA news agency.

Mohammad Reza Aref, the first deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian, criticized the lack of legal preparedness to address digital space issues and warned that continuing the current trend may lead to a crisis. He said that rulings are sometimes forcibly issued for the digital space based on the real space, which is unjustified. Aref ordered the formation of a permanent working group to gradually review and draft laws related to the digital space.

Yair Golan, leader of the Israeli Democratic Party, announced he will meet with three leaders of parties opposing Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday, 7 Aban, but did not disclose their names. These meetings occur as neither of the two main blocs in the Israeli parliamentary elections secured the 61 seats needed to form a government. Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, previously urged parties to negotiate to avoid a new election.

The Communications Office of the Turkish Presidency announced that Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke with Donald Trump about bilateral relations, developments in the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen, and the Ukraine war. Erdoğan said that as the Makkah Joint Defense Coalition, they closely monitor developments in the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen and strive to resolve these issues diplomatically.
With 86% of Israeli votes counted, Netanyahu's coalition leads with 53 seats. Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal revealed that the US has warned Gulf countries of an imminent intense war with Iran.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, stated that in one case, 34 people were tried over five days, 12 were sentenced to death, and seven have been executed so far. She said at least 34 people have been executed in connection with the protests of Dey 1401, and at least five were executed publicly. Thousands have been arrested on security charges, and families of the victims face pressure to remain silent.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) on Wednesday, 6 Aban, denied reports by media controlled by the Islamic Republic about commercial ships hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM stated that US forces have cleared all main maritime routes in this waterway of mines and these routes remain mine-free. CENTCOM emphasized that these claims are false and thousands of commercial ships have safely passed through these routes so far.
A video received shows that the fourth anniversary ceremony of Ali Fazeli and Hadi Chaksari, protesters killed in the Mahsa uprising, was held at their graves.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke by phone with Donald Trump about bilateral relations and regional and global issues. Erdogan emphasized efforts to strengthen cooperation on the occasion of the 100th anniversary of relations between the two countries. He also said Turkey is working within a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to resolve issues related to the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen and is ready to support efforts to revive diplomatic talks between Ukraine and Russia.

According to Oscar Puente, Spain's Minister of Transport, a Renfe train was allowed to continue moving despite a red signal caused by a computer communication failure, due to a wrong decision. In the collision of this train with another in Orda, 68 people were killed and dozens injured. This is the second deadly rail accident in Spain this year.

Axios reported, citing three American, Israeli, and regional sources, that Qatar, with the support of several regional countries, is trying to reach an agreement between Washington and Tehran to resume negotiations and prevent the outbreak of war after the US midterm elections. Qatar is trying to convince the Islamic Republic to allow International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors to visit the bombed nuclear facilities in Iran in exchange for reducing some US sanctions. Axios wrote that if diplomatic efforts fail, there is a possibility of a new round of US and Israeli attacks shortly after the midterm elections.

Milan and Inter clubs are scheduled to unveil the design of their new stadium in Milan tomorrow night. This project, which is expected to be completed by 2031, will have a capacity of 71,500 people, making it one of the five largest stadiums in Europe. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the design of the new stadium has been entrusted to 91-year-old architect Norman Foster and the Manica architecture firm.

The Dutch representative at the Third Committee meeting of the UN General Assembly called for the immediate halt of illegal executions, arbitrary detentions, and violence against the people of Iran. He referred to reports confirming widespread human rights violations by the Islamic Republic, including a significant increase in deadly force and mass arrests of protesters. He also expressed regret over the killing of civilians, including children, and called for a diplomatic solution to the war and full respect for international law by all parties, urging international support for holding perpetrators accountable.

The UK representative at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee stated that women and girls in Iran continue to face discrimination, arrest, and prosecution for not complying with mandatory hijab laws. He referred to reports of at least 34 protesters executed since Dey 1404 and called for an immediate halt to the executions. He also condemned the torture of detainees, widespread internet shutdowns, and the repression of ethnic and religious minorities in Iran.

The European Union representative announced that since Dey 1404, the EU has sanctioned 37 individuals and 9 entities for their role in human rights violations in Iran and is ready to take further actions if necessary. He said at the Third Committee meeting of the UN General Assembly that the Islamic Republic's security forces responded to protesters' demands with excessive violence and internal repression has increased. The EU representative called for an immediate halt to executions, release of arbitrary detainees, and an end to discrimination against women.

The Swiss representative at the Third Committee meeting of the UN General Assembly stated that some human rights violations in Iran since September 2025, according to the independent international fact-finding mission, constitute crimes against humanity. He condemned the use of the death penalty, called for a halt to executions, conversion of death sentences to other punishments, and support for human rights defenders. He also emphasized that Iranian authorities must respect due process and provide unhindered access to UN bodies.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the United States has informed several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short but intense military campaign after the US midterm elections. The US military is transferring a Patriot missile defense system from Texas to strengthen its missile defense capabilities and has withdrawn forces from bases near Iran. US forces in the region are replenishing ammunition supplies and fighter jets are preparing for attacks.
